purpose: Worldwide video-source ledger for extracting Saamaka lexical candidates without modifying the production dictionary automatically.

policy.note: A token heard or auto-transcribed once is never inserted directly into the SQLite dictionary.

sources.title: Saamaka Daka
evidence: Wikimedia Commons identifies the original YouTube video, title, publisher and date; screenshots were released from the video under CC BY.

sources.title: Saamaka Daka / Saamaka cultural event (title to verify from YouTube metadata)
evidence: Academic source cites this YouTube video while discussing the launch of Saamaka Daka in 2019.

sources.title: Maroon cultural event video (exact title to verify)
evidence: Academic source cites this video as an example of Maroon cultural offerings; Saamaka speech must be verified before lexical extraction.

sources.title: Banamba / Maroon dance event video (exact title to verify)
evidence: Academic source cites this video in discussion of Maroon dance contests. It may contain non-Saamaka varieties; speech must be language-identified first.

sources.title: Saamaka Marron Museum
evidence: 49-minute documentary made with Totomboti in Pikin Slee; description states that interviews and reactions from Saamaka participants were recorded, with Berry Vrede as interpreter/intermediary.

sources.title: Rastafari in Pikin Slee Suriname
evidence: Filmot indexes the YouTube video and exposes English subtitles.
The video is a portrait of Toya Saaki in Pikin Slee and credits the Saamaka Museum and inhabitants of Pikin Slee.
The subtitle track explicitly glosses the expression 'Gan Gado' as 'great God'.

sources.title: Neem as an Organic pesticide / Neem als Biologisch bestrijdingsmiddel
evidence: Filmot indexes the YouTube video with English subtitles.
The description/subtitles frame the content as ancient wisdom of the Saamaka tribe and discuss traditional agriculture.

sources.title: Team Bigi Boy's journey to the Upper Suriname River
sources.publisher: Local Content Suriname / Barend van Dijk
evidence: Local Content Suriname identifies the YouTube video as a journey to the lands of the Saamaka.

sources.title: The enabling power of participatory 3D mapping among the Saramaccan Peoples of Suriname — Saramaccan version
evidence: The publisher explicitly identifies this upload as the Saramaccan-language version of the participatory mapping documentary.

sources.title: The JESUS Film — Saramaccan [srm]
evidence: Scripture Earth explicitly labels the language Saramaccan, self-designation Saamáka, ISO srm.

sources.title: Bible videos in the Saramaccan language of Suriname
evidence: Scripture Earth exposes dozens of downloadable Saramaccan-language video segments from Matthew, Mark, Luke, Acts and John.

sources.title: Interview with Mr Lee in Saamaka Tongo
evidence: Community post by the interviewer explicitly identifies the interviewee as a Saamaka musician and says the interview is in Saamaka Tongo/Saramaccan.

sources.title: Life Of The Saamaka Maroons in 1928 / Djoeka re-edit
evidence: Source describes the 1928 Saamaka film as silent footage re-edited in 2010 and narrated by modern-day Saamaka Maroons.

sources.title: Sample video in Saramaccan
evidence: Omniglot labels an embedded sample video explicitly as Saramaccan and supplies sample Saramaccan sentences on the same language page.

sources.title: Saramacca [srm] audiovisual corpus

sources.title: La grammaire française en passant par la langue maternelle saamaka
evidence: Vimeo indexes this resource explicitly under a title identifying Saamaka as the learners' mother tongue; useful for bilingual grammar/lexicon evidence.

sources.title: Saamaka (English subtitles)
evidence: Vimeo states the 49-minute documentary records interviews, reactions, stories, music and everyday village/river sounds with Saamaka participants and English subtitles.

sources.title: Saamaka (Nederlands ondertiteld)
evidence: Dutch-subtitled edition of the Saamaka documentary; potentially useful as a second parallel-language alignment source.

sources.title: Saramacca [srm] MP4 audiovisual recordings
evidence: GRN explicitly identifies the language as Saramacca/Saamaka, ISO srm, and exposes an MP4 slideshow package plus links to additional Saramaccan video/audio sources.

sources.title: Saramaccan [srm] video/audio resource index
evidence: Resource index identifies Jesus Film, LUMO Gospel films, World Christian Videos, Faith Comes By Hearing and audio recordings for Saramaccan.

source_attestations.context_summary: Speaker explains that they call the Almighty 'Gan Gado'; English subtitle supplies the gloss 'great God'.

lexical_candidates.notes: Do not promote to confirmed until spelling is checked against a trusted Saamaka lexical source or a second independent attestation.

review_rules: Keep exact source URL and timecode for every candidate.
Do not infer spelling from sound alone when the transcription system is uncertain.
Separate Saamaka from Sranan Tongo, Ndyuka, Dutch, French and code-switching.
Compare every candidate against the embedded SQLite dictionary before proposing a new entry.
Prefer candidates attested in at least two independent sources or supported by a trusted dictionary/grammar.
Store uncertain forms as candidate/probable, never confirmed.

research_progress.discovery_note: Expanded beyond YouTube-only indexing when a source provides explicitly identified Saamaka/Saramaccan video; YouTube candidates remain tracked separately.
high_value_corpora: Scripture Earth srm video collection: dozens of explicitly Saramaccan-language segments
Participatory 3D mapping documentary: explicitly published Saramaccan version
Pikin Slee interviews and agriculture videos
Upper Suriname River travel/cultural videos pending language verification
next_steps: Prioritize sources with explicit ISO srm/Saramaccan labeling.
Obtain transcript or parallel Saamaka text before lexical extraction.
Deduplicate extracted forms against SQLite and existing candidate ledger.
Do not report an interim lexical count to the user before 100 sourced usable words/expressions.
research_progress.language_guard: Matawai/Matawari is not assumed interchangeable with Saamaka for lexical extraction; each recording must be language-identified.
research_progress.current_priority: Parallel-subtitled Saamaka material and explicitly ISO-srm-labelled audiovisual corpora before noisy auto-transcription.
